data.title: Ixigo Swings To Rs 63 Crore Profit In Q2
data.description:
Travel booking platform ixigo reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 63.42 crore for the September quarter, compared with a loss of Rs 3.46 crore a year earlier, helped by a partial stake sale in Freshbus and rapid growth in hotel bookings.

Revenue from operations rose 13 per cent year-on-year to Rs 320.96 crore in the second quarter of FY27, from Rs 284.23 crore in the corresponding period last year, according to a regulatory filing by Le Travenues Technology, which operates ixigo.

Total expenses increased to Rs 309.51 crore from Rs 291.89 crore a year earlier.

The company reported quarterly gross transaction value (GTV) of Rs 5,304 crore, up 22 per cent year-on-year, reflecting continued growth in its travel booking business.

Hotels was ixigo's fastest-growing business segment by GTV, with the metric rising 159 per cent year-on-year to Rs 111.34 crore. The September quarter marked the first time the company reported hotels as a separate business line.

In a joint statement, ixigo Group Chief Executive Officer Aloke Bajpai, Group Co-CEO Rajnish Kumar and Group Chief Financial Officer Saurabh Devendra Singh said the company had recorded its highest-ever quarterly profit after tax, aided by the partial sale of its stake in Freshbus.

The executives said the company would continue investing in hotels and artificial intelligence as key drivers of its long-term growth.

data.title: GPT Infraprojects Secures Rs 134 Cr Western Railway Signalling Contract
data.description:
The project covers four railway sections in Ratlam division, with completion scheduled within 548 days from the appointed date

GPT Infraprojects has secured a railway signalling contract worth Rs 134.11 crore, including GST, through its wholly-owned subsidiary Alcon Builders and Engineers Private Limited, the company said in a stock exchange filing.

The order has been awarded by the Chief Signal and Telecommunication Engineer, Western Railway, Ratlam Division, with the contract valued at Rs 113.65 crore excluding GST. The project covers signalling works across multiple double-line railway sections under the Ratlam division.

The scope includes survey, design, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of 4-Aspect Automatic Block Signalling with electronic interlocking and dual multi-section digital axle counters at auto huts. The contract also covers associated alterations to electronic interlocking systems at stations.

The works will be executed across the Nagda-Ujjain-Tajpur, Phanda-Sant Hirdaram Nagar, Ujjain-Karchha and Mangliyagaon-Indore double-line sections. GPT Infraprojects said the project is scheduled for completion within 548 days from the appointed date.

With the latest contract, GPT Infraprojects' net outstanding order book has reached Rs 5,651 crore. The company has recorded total order inflow of Rs 1,478 crore so far in fiscal 2027, strengthening its project pipeline for the year.

GPT Infraprojects operates through infrastructure and sleeper segments, with its infrastructure business covering civil and railway projects. Its activities include bridges, road-over-bridges and railway signalling works, alongside concrete sleeper manufacturing.

Railway Business Gains

The company manufactures concrete sleepers for railway projects through facilities in West Bengal, South Africa, Namibia and Ghana. Its operations therefore span both infrastructure execution and railway component manufacturing across India and overseas markets.

Shares of GPT Infraprojects ended nearly 1 per cent higher on the day. The stock has gained around 15 per cent so far this year, as the company continues to build its order pipeline across railway and infrastructure projects.

data.title: RailTel Secures Rs 186.5 Cr Orders For Recruitment, Cybersecurity
data.description:
The larger project runs through 2031 for railway recruitment services, while the second covers technology and cybersecurity support through 2029

RailTel Corporation of India has secured two work orders worth a combined Rs 186.51 crore, including a Rs 167.52 crore contract from the Railway Recruitment Board (RRB), Secunderabad, for recruitment examination services.

The company received both orders on 16 October, according to its regulatory filing. The contracts cover recruitment examination management as well as IT infrastructure and cybersecurity solutions, further adding to RailTel's project pipeline.

The larger order, estimated at Rs 167.52 crore excluding taxes, covers AM-RMS services for the pre-examination and post-examination stages of RRB recruitment conducted through various Centralised Employment Notifications (CENs).

The contract is scheduled to remain valid until 15 October 2031, giving RailTel a long-term engagement to provide services associated with the recruitment examination process conducted by the railway recruitment board.

IT Infrastructure Order

The second order, worth Rs 18.99 crore including taxes, has been awarded by Health Insurance TPA of India Ltd for IT infrastructure and cybersecurity solutions. The three-year contract is scheduled to run until 16 October 2029, expanding RailTel's recent project wins across technology, digital infrastructure and cybersecurity-related services.

The latest contracts follow several orders secured by RailTel in recent months, covering digital governance, telecom infrastructure and technology services for government and public-sector clients.

On 13 October, RailTel received a Rs 49 crore order, including taxes, from the Odisha government's Higher Education Department to develop 83 digital application modules under a Comprehensive Digital Governance Platform.

In August, the company secured a Rs 165 crore contract, including taxes, from Western Coalfields to establish a Multiprotocol Label Switching Virtual Private Network on a rental basis for 60 months.

The Western Coalfields contract is scheduled to continue until 20 September 2031. RailTel also received a Rs 166.8 crore order from the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation in August to extend an existing Infrastructure-as-a-Service arrangement through RailTel by one year.

The EPFO contract includes additional components and is scheduled to run until 9 February 2027. RailTel shares closed at Rs 255.05 on the BSE on 16 October, rising 0.57 per cent during the session.

data.title: Nifty soars 2.8% this week: What lies ahead for Dalal Street? - Experts decode 5 triggers, key levels for next week
data.description:
Stock Market Outlook, Oct. 17 -- Indian equities staged a strong comeback this week, with the Nifty 50 rising 2.77% and the Sensex surging 3.11%, as renewed buying in information technology (IT) stocks, easing global bond-yield pressures and resilient domestic institutional inflows lifted investor sentiment.

Both benchmarks also extended their gains for a second consecutive session on Friday, strengthening hopes of a recovery after the recent market correction.

On Friday, the Sensex climbed 413.66 points, or 0.56%, to close at 74,729.27 on Friday, while the Nifty advanced 148.80 points, or 0.65%, to settle at 23,146.15. For the week, the Sensex gained 2,256.94 points, while the Nifty added 625.7 points.

However, the rally faces several tests, including whether earnings growth broadens beyond IT, foreign investor selling eases further and the Nifty breaks through immediate resistance. Market experts believe investors should remain selective as global macroeconomic uncertainty and domestic inflation concerns persist.

The September-quarter earnings season will remain a major driver of market sentiment. Investors will assess whether companies can deliver stronger revenue growth and margins across banking, consumption and industrials, rather than relying primarily on IT stocks to sustain the recovery.

Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments Limited, said, "The sustainability of the recovery will hinge on earnings growth broadening beyond IT, with revenue and margin delivery across financials, consumption and industrials under close scrutiny."

Foreign institutional investor (FII) flows remain a key variable for the market. While foreign portfolio outflows have moderated, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continue to provide support through sustained buying.

Ravi Singh, Chief Research Officer at Master Capital Services Ltd, said weekly foreign portfolio outflows narrowed to Rs.8,991 crore, while domestic institutional investors purchased approximately Rs.7,813 crore worth of shares. Any further moderation in foreign selling could help stabilise the indices.

Global monetary policy expectations, geopolitical developments and energy prices will remain important determinants of investor appetite for equities. Higher crude prices can fuel inflation, while rising bond yields may increase the relative attractiveness of fixed-income investments and put pressure on equity valuations.

Ajit Mishra, SVP - Research, Religare Broking. noted, "Global markets are currently in a transition phase. Major central banks, including the US Federal Reserve, have started moving towards an easier monetary policy stance, while growth remains subdued across regions such as Europe and China."

IT shares have been a key driver of the recent recovery, supported by a shift in global investor positioning following a sell-off in international AI and semiconductor stocks. Singh attributed the buying interest in Indian IT services companies to concerns over elevated valuations and delayed monetisation cycles among global AI hardware and chipmakers.

Indian IT companies, with their established execution capabilities and comparatively attractive valuations, have benefited from this rotation. Investors will watch whether the momentum continues or broadens to other sectors.

The Nifty has rebounded from support near 22,200 and reclaimed its 21-day exponential moving average (EMA) around 22,900, indicating improving near-term momentum. However, the index must overcome immediate resistance to extend its recovery.

Singh said, "As long as Nifty sustains above this level, buying interest is likely to persist, making a buy-on-dips strategy prudent. On the upside, the 55-day EMA near 23360 remains the immediate resistance."

The near-term technical setup has improved, but experts favour selective stock picking over aggressive index-level positioning.

The Nifty's immediate resistance is around 23,360, corresponding to its 55-day EMA. A decisive breakout could open the way towards 23,600, according to Singh's technical assessment. On the downside, the 21-day EMA near 22,900 is an important level to defend, while 22,200 remains a significant support zone.

Mishra's medium-term assessment is constructive, subject to an improvement in corporate earnings. The analyst said, "Immediate resistance sits near 23,800-24,000; a sustained breakout above that could set up a retest of the 26,350-26,500 zone over 6 months, contingent on earnings acceleration."

The analyst identified 23,000 as immediate support, followed by the 52-week low near 22,182. These are medium-term levels and should be distinguished from the nearer-term technical markers highlighted by Singh.

For investors, a staggered buy-on-dips approach may be preferable to chasing sharp rallies, provided key support levels hold. Companies with sustainable earnings growth, strong balance sheets and reasonable valuations are likely to offer a more disciplined route through continued volatility.

India's October PMI, US jobless claims, Japan's inflation data, Corporate earnings and management commentary, rupee, crude oil bond yields, and FII and DII activity will be closely watched next week.

Nair cautioned that the market was likely to remain selective and earnings-driven amid elevated inflation and a tightening policy bias. The next leg of the rally will depend on whether corporate earnings support current valuations and the Nifty can clear resistance while holding its recently reclaimed support levels.
